newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN FIGHT BACK AFTER COLLAPSE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN FIGHT BACK AFTER COLLAPSE.

text.p: Pakistan recovered from a dismal top-order collapse to beat Australia by 29 runs on Tuesday in a low-scoring World Series limited overs match dominated by bowlers.
Chasing Pakistan's seemingly inadequate total of 149 all out, Australia were dismissed for a paltry 120 on a lively wicket at Bellerive Oval.

It was a remarkable performance by Pakistan after their top three batsmen -- Aamir Sohail, Zahoor Elahi and Ijaz Ahmed -- were all dismissed for ducks to leave them in disarray at seven for three early on.
But a spirited innings of 54, the highest score of the match, by Mohammad Wasim lifted his side to a respectable total that ultimately proved enough for his bowlers to defend.
Pakistan captain Wasim Akram and fellow fast bowler Mohammad Zahid fully exploited a pitch that offered both movement and variable bounce to dismiss Australia in 41.3 overs.
At times, the pitch was almost unplayable as deliveries reared alarmingly off a length, troubling all the batsmen.
The final result justified Akram's decision to bat in overcast conditions favourable to the bowlers after winning the toss in front of a record crowd of 11,541 in Hobart.
It also leaves the Australians in danger of not making the World Series finals.
Pakistan joined West Indies on six points from five games at the top of the table in the triangular tournament.

Australia, who lost ten of their last 12 one-day matches at home and abroad, are on four points but have played one more game than their rivals. The Australians have two more games to play while the other two both have three left.
Zahid bowled at extreme pace to remove all-rounder Greg Blewett and leg-spinner Shane Warne, compensating for his occasional lack of control that cost three wides and six no-balls.
Akram, in contrast, combined his menance with relentless accuracy to claim three for 13 in eight overs.
Australia's poor batting display was highlighted by the fact that none of their players managed to score more runs than the extras total of 28.
